title: Shadow Runner Load Test Plan (Sheet) — Capacity Budgets, Matrix, and Results
content:
Doc purpose
- Validate Shadow Runner can execute production-shaped shadow traffic without impacting primary serving SLOs.
- Confirm capacity budgets + rate limits/backpressure behave as designed under misconfig and burst.
- Establish pass/fail gates for beta rollout (per-region) and alert thresholds.

Owner / DRI (SRE)
- DRI: Sean Gallagher
- On-call/runbook owner: Rafael Mendes
- Capacity coordination: Vanessa Ortiz
- Autoscaling/guardrails: Keiko Yamamoto
- Telemetry support: Logan Wright

Test environment
- Staging/perf: perf-canary + synthetic traffic generator, plus “production mirror (no user impact)” where explicitly noted.
- Regions: us-east-1, us-west-2, eu-west-1 (beta order).
- Shadow target(s): candidate model/version(s) configured in RoutePolicy shadow_traffic targets.
- Shadow runner queue: async worker pool (isolated from primary path).

Key invariants (must hold)
1) Primary path p99 latency: no regression beyond budget (see Pass/Fail).
2) Shadow runner failures must not fail the primary request (error isolation).
3) Capacity budgets must enforce shadow drops/backpressure before impacting primary.
4) Kill switch disables shadow execution within 60s globally, without deploy.
5) Telemetry/cardinality within guardrails (no label explosion).

Baseline assumptions (used for expected load math)
- Baseline primary traffic: 500 RPS per region for the target route(s) under test (adjust per run).
- Average input tokens: 650, output tokens: 250 (streaming on primary; shadow is non-streaming by default).
- Shadow targets per request: 1 for MVP (optional 2-target test for future).
- Concurrency estimate: 1 shadow request ~= 1 primary request worth of GPU time (worst-case) unless quantized target.


TAB: Pass/Fail Criteria
Metric	Target	Notes / how measured
Primary p99 latency delta	<= +0.0% in steady-state; <= +1.0% during 5-min ramp windows	Measured at gateway + runtime. This is strict; any sustained regression is a FAIL.
Primary error rate (5xx)	No increase attributable to shadow	Compare against baseline + correlate with shadow queue depth.
Shadow queue depth	< 70% of max_depth sustained for >10 min	If sustained >70% => FAIL unless expected in “over-budget” scenarios.
Shadow drop rate (budgeted)	<= 2% in “in-budget” tests	Drops are OK when intentionally over budget; must be visible in metrics.
Shadow execution success rate	>= 98% (excluding explicit timeouts/cancels)	Includes judge calls where enabled.
Shadow worker CPU/mem stability	No monotonic growth; no OOM/restarts	We saw a leak in early beta; verify fixed (ref PR-48363 if applicable).
Kill switch efficacy	< 60s to stop new shadow executions	Validated via dashboard + log/metric.
Telemetry latency	< 2 min to aggregated metrics availability	For Console dashboards; raw events can be near-real-time.
Cardinality guardrails	No new high-cardinality tags; time series count within budget	Validate per ENG-2435.

Notes
- “Primary p99 unchanged” is the gating criterion for moving from staging to limited production mirroring.
- Shadow-only SLOs (queue depth, error rate) can be violated in explicitly marked stress scenarios as long as primary remains stable.

Operator notes (for each run)
- Validate config: RoutePolicy shadow_traffic.{enabled,sample_rate,target(s),budget} + global kill switch default OFF.
- Confirm rate-limit/backpressure settings (PR-48275): per-region cap, queue max_depth, drop-on-overflow semantics.
- Confirm dashboards: shadow runner overview (queue depth, drops, exec latency) + primary SLO charts aligned in same timeframe.


TAB: Expected Utilization / Capacity Budget (rough)
Field	Value	Notes
Shadow budget default (beta)	<= 3% of primary GPU time per route per region	Goal is “small but meaningful” sampling without infra surprises
Shadow hard cap (safety)	10% (enforced via rate limiting/backpressure)	Anything above should drop shadow work first
Queue depth default	10,000	Tune per region based on memory + burst tolerance
Worker pool size	Autoscaled to keep queue < 50% depth	If autoscaling lags, allow drops vs primary impact
Expected shadow GPU delta at 1%	~2–4% utilization	Overhead includes scheduling + tokenization + logging
Expected shadow GPU delta at 10%	~15–22% utilization	Non-linearities possible due to batch fragmentation

Caveats
- If shadow target model is larger than primary, capacity multipliers apply (update expected numbers per route).
- Judge calls add CPU + network + additional LLM inference if judge model hosted internally; treat LT-09 as separate budget.

TAB: Notes / How to Run (operator checklist)
Pre-flight
- Confirm target route(s) + model pair and that primary path is stable (no ongoing incident).
- Ensure dashboards are pinned: primary latency, primary error rate, GPU util, shadow queue depth, shadow drops, shadow exec latency.
- Confirm global kill switch endpoint access and permissions (on-call only).
- Confirm per-route disable knob works in control plane and does not require deploy.

Run steps (per scenario)
1) Apply config (shadow sample %, target(s), budgets) in the control plane.
2) Ramp traffic generator to target RPS (or enable controlled production mirror if approved).
3) Hold steady 20–30 min.
4) Capture screenshots / saved graph links.
5) Record results row.

Abort conditions (stop test immediately)
- Any sustained primary p99 regression >1% over 5 min.
- Any increase in primary 5xx correlated with shadow enabling.
- GPU utilization exceeds safe operating threshold for region (see capacity sheet).

Post-run
- Reset sampling to 0% or safe default.
- Verify queue drains to baseline.
- Post summary in #eng-sre and tag DRI owners for follow-ups.
